sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Anirudh Kumar Upadhyay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Dileep Kumar Srivastava
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1.
List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Anirudh Kumar Upadhyay, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Dileep Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the informant, Sri Sakeel Ahmad, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.

3. The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for anticipatory bail in Case Crime No.422 of 2007, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468 and 471 I.P.C., Police Station Sonhan, District Basti, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Krishna Gopal vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to be the head master in the school concerned which was unaided institution since 1978.

In the year 2006, the school was assigned the category of aided institution, for which M.R. list was to be given to the authorities regarding the employees, in which the applicant is stated to have not cooperated, as such the institution could not be granted aid.
The FIR was instituted on 19.07.2007.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He had been working pro bono and had not charged a single penny from the institution for such a long period of time.
Learned counsel has further stated that the applicant is a bona fide person and has co-operated during trial.
There are no criminal antecedents of the applicant.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the informant and learned A.G.A. have vehemently opposed the anticipatory bail application on the ground that the applicant is not cooperating with trial as already the final report (charge-sheet) has been submitted in the year 2008 and subsequent to it, the applicant had challenged it by filing a petition U/s 482 Cr.P.C., which was dismissed and a direction was given him to appear and file a discharge application.

Subsequent to it, discharge application was filed, which was dismissed by the court concerned in the year 2016 and the applicant had challenged the rejection of discharge application by filing Criminal Revision No. 1748 of 2016 before this Court and the same was disposed of vide order dated 08.08.2022 and the applicant was directed to appear and apply for bail in the light of the judgment of Apex Court passed in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825, as such the applicant is not entitled for anticipatory bail.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 SCC OnLine SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In rebuttal, learned counsel for the applicant has stated that in the same revision the applicant was granted stay vide order dated 09.06.2016 and has not misused it, but subsequent to it, the revision has been disposed of.

8. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the applicant had time and again taken recourse to this Court by filing petitions U/s 482 Cr.P.C. and U/s 397 Cr.P.C., I do not find it a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
9. The present anticipatory bail application is hereby found devoid of merits and is accordingly rejected.

10. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of anticipatory bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

(Krishan Pahal, J.) Order Date :- 21.7.2023 Ravi Kant  Krishna Gopal vs State Of U.P. And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169127176/
